sources.entry: CookCLI - Command-line tool for automating meal planning and shopping with Cooklang recipes, scriptable for UNIX workflows, includes web server. (Source Code) MIT Rust

summary.one_liner: CookCLI is a command-line tool for working with Cooklang recipe files, covering shopping lists, meal plans, reports, search, pantry tracking and an optional web server for browsing recipes.
summary.what_it_does: CookCLI provides a set of "cook" subcommands for parsing and displaying Cooklang recipes, scaling quantities, and exporting recipes as JSON or Markdown. It generates shopping lists from one or more recipes, combining ingredients and grouping them by store aisle according to an aisle.conf file. Menu files let you plan meals by day and meal and produce a combined shopping list for the plan. The cook server command runs a web UI for browsing recipes from any device, and cook build web generates a static website from a recipe folder. Other commands cover recipe search, validation via cook doctor, pantry inventory with low-stock and expiry tracking (pantry items are excluded from shopping lists), custom templated reports, and importing recipes from websites (which requires an OPENAI_API_KEY). Optional sign-in for the server and cloud sync via cook login are also described.
use_cases: plan weekly meals with menu files
browse a personal recipe collection in a web browser
validate and maintain a Cooklang recipe folder
track pantry stock and expiring ingredients
scale recipe quantities from the command line
notable: Follows the UNIX philosophy: commands are scriptable and pipe-friendly, e.g. cook search chicken | xargs cook shopping-list
Menu files (.menu) combine recipes and inline ingredients into a day-by-day plan with a merged shopping list
Optional Cargo features (server, import, lsp, sync, self-update) shrink the binary from about 23 MB to about 9 MB
Pre-built binaries for Linux, macOS, Windows, FreeBSD, plus RPM and .deb packages
Pantry tracking via pantry.conf excludes items already at home from shopping lists
caveats: Building from source needs Node.js for CSS/JS assets, or a release source tarball that bundles them; building with cargo needs a few GB of RAM and disk
Some features need external services or accounts: cook import needs OPENAI_API_KEY or cook.md (Cook Basic), and sync needs Cook Cloud (Cook Basic)
Without users configured, anyone who can reach cook server can change recipes; sign-in must be set up explicitly
